newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end down, spotlight on HPI,Marzotto.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end down, spotlight on HPI,Marzotto.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower after a lacklustre session on Monday livened up only by interest in industrial holding group HPI and textile group Marzotto after weekend news of their merger.
Traders said sentiment was weighed down by persistent worries over Italian political situation and EMU and the lira was a touch weaker against the mark.
Traded volume was estimated sharply lower at around 778 billion lire against Friday's 1.08 trillion lire.
HPI, making its bourse debut, ended at 1,106 lire against the bourse council valuation of 1,050. Marzotto closed 6.02 percent firmer at 14,260 lire.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.85 percent down at 12,126 but off a session low of 12,079. The Mib30 blue chip index closed off 0.93 percent at 17,991.
Energy group ENI closed 1.24 percent down at 8,526 lire and Fiat slipped 0.46 percent to 5,463 after good car sales figures for February but which were in line with expectations.
Olivetti lost 0.21 percent to 627.3 and Pirelli SpA slipped 0.84 percent to 3,670 after performing well early on after brokers' buy recommendations last week.
In weak telecoms, Stet holding ended 0.56 percent off at 7,971, Telecom Italia lost 0.23 percent to 4,409 and mobile phone operator TIM lost 1.16 percent to 4,441.
Banks and insurances were mostly weaker. Benetton group lost 1.78 percent to 20,544 but Bulgari gained 0.68 pct to 30,713.
